items.exampleCN: 窃贼盯上了空置的房屋。

items.example: Car theft fell sharply this year.
He thieved his way through the fair.
items.exampleCN: 他在集市上一路顺手牵羊。

items.meaningCN: 盗窃癖（希腊词根 klept 同义不同源）
items.example: Kleptomania is an illness, not a choice.
items.exampleCN: 盗窃癖是疾病，不是选择。

items.meaning: breaking into a building to steal
items.example: Burglary rose in the holiday season.
The robbery lasted ninety seconds.
The pilferer took only stationery.
items.exampleCN: 那个顺手牵羊者只拿了文具。

items.meaning: a thief who works in crowds
items.example: Beware of pickpockets on the bus.

definition_zh: 薄的；细的；瘦的；稀疏的；稀薄的；（动词）使变薄；变稀
definition_en: having a small distance between two sides, little flesh, or few things in a space; to make or become thinner
core_image: 两指间只剩一张纸的缝隙：几乎没有厚度
scene: 减肥半年后,她的旧戒指又合手了。After half a year of dieting, her wrists grew thin and the old ring fit again.
sceneCN: 这里 thin 是「变瘦」（第 3 个义项：身上脂肪减少）；句意：节食半年后她的手腕变细，旧戒指又能戴上了。

derivatives.zh: 薄薄地；稀疏地（thin 加副词后缀 -ly）
薄；细；瘦；稀（thin 加名词后缀 -ness）
稀释剂（比较级转名词，指油漆稀释液）
稀疏下来（短语动词，指密度降低）

senses.title: Small distance between surfaces
senses.definition: having a small distance between two opposite sides or surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 两个相对面之间的距离很小
senses.example: She cut the bread into thin slices.
senses.exampleCN: 她把面包切成薄片。
senses.why: The direct opposite of thick: where thick fills the gap, thin almost erases it.
senses.whyCN: thick 的直接反义：thick 填满间隙，thin 几乎把间隙抹掉。

senses.title: Sparse or scattered
senses.definition: with few things or people in a space; not dense
senses.definitionCN: 空间中的人或物很少；不稠密
senses.example: The crowd was thin after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜后人群稀稀落落。
senses.why: What is true of a slice is true of a group: take parts away, and what remains spreads thin.
senses.whyCN: 对薄片成立的道理对人群同样成立：抽走一部分，剩下的就摊薄了。

senses.title: Having little flesh
senses.definition: (of a person or animal) having little fat or flesh on the body
senses.definitionCN: 指人或动物身上脂肪或肉少
senses.example: He looked thin after weeks of illness.
senses.exampleCN: 病了几周后他看上去瘦了。
senses.why: The body itself is read as a slab: fat gives it thickness, and losing fat makes the body thin.
senses.whyCN: 身体本身被当作一块板来读：脂肪给身体厚度，减去脂肪身体就 thin 了。

senses.title: Weak or not convincing
senses.definition: lacking force, substance, or believability, as an excuse or evidence
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏力度、内容或可信度，如借口或证据
senses.example: The committee dismissed his excuse as thin.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会认为他的借口站不住脚。
senses.why: An argument with little substance is a slice with little substance: almost nothing between its two faces.
senses.whyCN: 内容贫乏的论证如同内容贫乏的薄片：两面之间几乎什么都没有。

senses.title: To become or make thinner
senses.definition: to make or become thinner, less dense, or less crowded
senses.definitionCN: 使变薄、变稀或变疏，或自身变得如此
senses.example: The fog thinned as the sun climbed.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳升高后雾渐渐变薄。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a verb without any new ending: English lets qualities move on their own.
senses.whyCN: 形容词不加任何新词尾直接变成动词：英语允许性质自己走动。

intro.en: Thin is a native Germanic word, twin of thick in daily life and nearly twin in history: both descend from one ancient root family of density words.
intro.cn: thin 是日耳曼本土词，在日常生活中与 thick 成对，历史上也几乎是孪生：两者都出自同一古老的密度词族。

items.en: The common Germanic root Thinn, generally reconstructed as meaning stretched or drawn thin, spread across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 公认日耳曼词根一般重构为 Thinn，意为「拉伸变细」，遍布各日耳曼语言。

items.en: Old English Tinne (or thinne) served for flat things, slender bodies, and sparse crowds alike.
items.cn: 古英语 Tinne (or thinne) 兼指扁平物、细瘦身形与稀疏人群。

items.en: Norse Thunn(or thynn)r reinforced the northern forms, as with its partner thick.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 Thunn(or thynnr) 与它的搭档 thick 一样加强了北方形式。

items.en: Middle English thinne settled the spelling, and the verb use without endings grew common in craft talk.
items.cn: 中古英语 thinne 固定拼写，无词尾的动词用法在手工艺语中渐趋常用。

items.en: Modern English doubled the n before -er, -est and -ing (thinner, thinned, thinning) and spread the word into science and slang alike.
items.cn: 现代英语在 -er、-est、-ing 前双写 n（thinner、thinned、thinning），并把这个词推广到科学与俚语。

note.en: The first group is the thin family; the second compares words of slenderness and weakness.
note.cn: 第一组是 thin 词族；第二组比较表示纤细与贫弱的词。

entries.definition: in a thin way; the adverb of thin
entries.definitionCN: 薄薄地；稀疏地（thin 的副词）

entries.definition: the comparative of thin, and also a liquid that dilutes paint
entries.definitionCN: 更瘦/更薄；也是稀释油漆的稀释剂

entries.definition: an object; only one letter from thin, unrelated in meaning
entries.definitionCN: 东西；与 thin 仅一字母之差，词义无关

entries.definition: attractively thin and graceful
entries.definitionCN: 苗条修长的；带优雅意味的 thin

entries.definition: very thin in an unattractive or joking way
entries.definitionCN: 皮包骨的；口语化、略含贬义的 thin

entries.definition: thinly scattered; the formal partner of the sparse sense
entries.definitionCN: 稀疏的；thin 稀疏义的正式对应词

normalIntro.en: Real hooks: the thick-thin pair, the doubled n in thinning, and the verb without an ending.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：thick-thin 成对、thinning 的双写 n、以及不加词尾的动词用法。

normal.en: Thick and thin are twins: one fills, one empties.
normal.cn: thick 与 thin 是孪生：一个填满，一个抽空。

normal.en: Thin, thinner, thinnest: double the n when a vowel follows.
normal.cn: thin, thinner, thinnest：后接元音时双写 n。

normal.en: On thin ice: standing where the layer is too weak to hold you.
normal.cn: on thin ice：站在薄得撑不住你的冰面上。

normal.en: Vanish into thin air: become as insubstantial as the fog.
normal.cn: vanish into thin air：变得像雾一样无影无踪。

normal.en: The fog thinned: the adjective works as a verb with no new ending.
normal.cn: 雾变薄了：形容词不加词尾直接当动词用。

abstract.en: Thin is the world after something has been taken away.
abstract.cn: thin 是被拿走某物之后的世界。

abstract.en: A thin excuse has nothing between its two faces.
abstract.cn: 站不住脚的借口，两面之间空无一物。

abstract.en: Where thick protects, thin exposes.
abstract.cn: thick 庇护之处，thin 无所遮拦。

examples.en: The ice on the lake is still too thin to walk on.
examples.cn: 湖面的冰还太薄，不能上人。

examples.en: She stirred the paint with a little thinner.
examples.cn: 她往颜料里加了点稀释剂搅拌。

examples.en: His voice sounded thin over the bad phone line.
examples.cn: 电话线路不好，他的声音听上去单薄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「希恩」——瘦得让人希罕又心疼 → thin 瘦的；薄的

root: 日耳曼本土词：词根一般重构为 Thinn「拉伸变细」→ 古英语 Tinne (or thinne)；与德语 dunn、荷兰语 dun 同源，与 thick 同属本土密度词族。

sensesIntro.en: Thin starts as the small measure of a slice, spreads to sparse crowds and lean bodies, then to weak arguments, and finally works as its own verb.
sensesIntro.cn: thin 从薄片的厚度出发，延伸到稀疏的人群与清瘦的身形、单薄的论证，最后亲自动词化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: almost nothing between two faces, the gap nearly gone.
core.cn: 核心意象：两面之间几乎没有东西，间隙近乎消失。

branches.en: The small physical measure.
branches.cn: 小的物理量度。

branches.en: Few things spread over a space.
branches.cn: 稀疏地摊在一个空间里。

branches.en: The body read as a slab without its fat layer.
branches.cn: 被读作失去脂肪层的身体。

branches.en: Arguments and evidence that cannot carry weight.
branches.cn: 承受不了重量的论证与证据。

branches.en: The word acts on the world instead of describing it.
branches.cn: 这个词开始改造世界，而不只是描述世界。

intro.en: Thin takes small native endings and doubles its n when they begin with a vowel; the verb needs no ending at all.
intro.cn: thin 加本土小词尾，且当词尾以元音开头时双写 n；动词化则完全不需要词尾。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source; the family is native Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语来源；词族为日耳曼本土，拉丁词条留空。

items.meaning: more thin; also a paint-diluting liquid
items.example: Add thinner to the paint.
The thinnest wire carries the signal.

items.exampleCN: 臭氧层变薄令科学家担忧。

items.meaning: in a thin or weak way
items.example: He smiled thinly at the joke.
items.exampleCN: 听到这个笑话他勉强笑了笑。

items.example: The thinness of the walls surprised them.

items.meaningCN: 脱脂的（fat 词族的对照）
items.example: She bought fat-free yogurt.
A skinny cat waited by the bin.
items.exampleCN: 一只瘦猫在垃圾桶旁等着。

definition_zh: 东西；事物；事情；事件；情况（复数）
definition_en: an object that is not named, an event or situation, or matters in general
core_image: 一个装着说不清之物的口袋：指哪算哪
scene: 搬家那天,纸箱堆满了走廊。The first thing to pack was the bookshelf.
sceneCN: 这里 thing 是「东西、物件」（第 1 个义项：泛指物品）；句意：头一件要打包的东西是书架。

任何事物（any 加 thing 构成的复合代词）

senses.title: An object without a name
senses.definition: an object whose name is not known, not stated, or not worth stating
senses.definitionCN: 名称未知、不必说或不愿说的物品
senses.example: What is that thing on the shelf?
senses.exampleCN: 架子上那个东西是什么？
senses.why: When a name is missing, the word opens an empty box and points: whatever fits inside becomes the thing.
senses.whyCN: 名字缺席时，这个词打开一只空盒一指：装得进去的都算这个 thing。

senses.title: An event or matter
senses.definition: an event, an action, or a matter to be dealt with
senses.definitionCN: 发生的事、要做的事或待处理的事项
senses.example: There is one more thing to discuss before lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 午饭前还有一件事要讨论。
senses.why: The empty box works for happenings too: an unnamed event slides in as easily as an unnamed object.
senses.whyCN: 空盒同样装得下发生的事：没点名的事件和没点名的物件一样容易滑进去。

senses.title: Situations in general
senses.definition: the general state of affairs, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 事情的总体状况，通常用复数
senses.example: Things have changed a lot since last year.
senses.exampleCN: 自去年以来情况变化很大。
senses.why: Piled together, single matters become the whole situation; the plural turns many boxes into one landscape.
senses.whyCN: 许多单件事堆在一起便成了整个局面；复数把许多盒子合成一幅风景。

senses.title: Personal possessions
senses.definition: the objects that belong to someone, especially clothes and personal items
senses.definitionCN: 属于某人的物品，尤指衣物与个人用品
senses.example: Gather your things and leave quietly.
senses.exampleCN: 收拾好你的东西，安静地离开。
senses.why: A person's life scatters into objects; the plural thing gathers the scattered self back into a bag.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的生活散落为物品；复数的 things 把散落的自己收进一只袋子。

senses.title: A creature, said with feeling
senses.definition: a living being, spoken of with affection, pity, or annoyance instead of a name
senses.definitionCN: 以怜爱、怜悯或嗔怪的口吻称呼的生灵
senses.example: You poor thing, come inside and warm up.
senses.exampleCN: 你这可怜的小东西，进来暖和暖和。
senses.why: When feeling replaces the name, even a person can be packed into the empty box, softly or sharply.
senses.whyCN: 当情感替代名字，连人也能被装进那只空盒——或温柔，或带刺。

intro.en: Thing is one of the oldest words in English, and its ancient Germanic ancestor meant not an object but an assembly: the meeting where matters were decided.
intro.cn: thing 是英语最古老的词之一；它的日耳曼远祖本义不是「物」而是「集会」——裁决事务的会议。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic root Thingam meant a set time or an assembly for deciding matters; the Icelandic parliament is still the Althing.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼词根一般认为意为「约定的时刻或裁决事务的集会」；冰岛议会至今仍叫 Althing。

items.en: Old English Thing meant a meeting, a matter under discussion, and by extension an affair or an object concerned with it.
items.cn: 古英语 Thing 意为集会、议事之事项，进而指相关的事务或物件。

items.en: Norse Thing, meaning assembly, reinforced the English word in the north, where place names like Thingwall keep the meeting sense.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 Thing（集会）在北方加强了英语本词；Thingwall 之类的地名保留了「会议」义。

items.en: Middle English thing widened into the great all-purpose noun: any object, any event, any matter.
items.cn: 中古英语 thing 扩展为万能名词：任何物件、任何事件、任何事项。

items.en: Modern English multiplied the compounds something, anything, everything, nothing, making thing the backbone of English indefinites.
items.cn: 现代英语衍生出 something、anything、everything、nothing，使 thing 成为英语不定代词的骨架。

note.en: The first group holds the -thing compounds; the second compares the general nouns of object and matter.
note.cn: 第一组是 -thing 复合代词；第二组比较指物与指事的泛称名词。

entries.definition: an unspecified object or matter
entries.definitionCN: 某物；某事（some 加 thing）

entries.definition: not anything; the empty end of the -thing family
entries.definitionCN: 什么也没有（-thing 家族的空端）

entries.definition: of small thickness; one letter from thing, no relation in meaning
entries.definitionCN: 薄的；与 thing 仅一字母之差，词义无关

entries.definition: a material thing that can be seen and touched
entries.definitionCN: 物体；可见可触的具体物件

entries.definition: a subject or situation to deal with; more formal than thing
entries.definitionCN: 事项；比 thing 更正式的事务用词

entries.definition: things in a mass; the casual spoken partner
entries.definitionCN: 东西；口语中随意的对应词

normalIntro.en: Real hooks: the ancient assembly sense, the -thing compounds, and the plural of situations.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：古老的集会义、-thing 复合词、以及表情况的复数用法。

normal.en: Thing once meant a meeting; Iceland's parliament, the Althing, keeps the old sense.
normal.cn: thing 曾指集会；冰岛议会 Althing 保留着古义。

normal.en: Something, anything, everything, nothing: four compounds, one backbone.
normal.cn: something、anything、everything、nothing：四个复合词，同一根骨架。

normal.en: Things have changed: the plural speaks of the whole situation.
normal.cn: things have changed：复数谈论整个局面。

normal.en: Pack your things: possessions gather under the same word.
normal.cn: pack your things：随身物品也归同一个词。

normal.en: You poor thing: feeling replaces the name.
normal.cn: you poor thing：情感替代了名字。

abstract.en: Thing is the box language opens when the name is missing.
abstract.cn: thing 是名字缺席时语言打开的盒子。

abstract.en: Every meeting of people is a meeting of things to decide.
abstract.cn: 人的集会，就是待决之事项的集会。

abstract.en: A life can be packed into things; a day can be packed into things to do.
abstract.cn: 生活可以装进物品，一天可以装进待办之事。

examples.en: The important thing is to arrive on time.
examples.cn: 重要的是准时到达。

examples.en: Things are getting better between them.
examples.cn: 他们之间的关系正在好转。

examples.en: She packed her things and moved out.
examples.cn: 她收拾好东西搬了出去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯英」——说不清是啥的东西,一声「斯英?」了之 → thing 东西

root: 日耳曼本土词：词根一般指「集会、议事事项」（冰岛议会 Althing 存古）→ 古英语 Thing「会议；事务；物件」，经古诺斯语强化；无拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: Thing is the all-purpose box: it holds unnamed objects, unnamed events, the whole situation, a person's belongings, and even a person spoken of with feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: thing 是万能的盒子：装得下没点名的物件与事件、整个局面、一个人的随身物品，甚至一个被带着情感称呼的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty box that points instead of naming.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只不称呼而只指示的空盒。

branches.en: The object whose name is withheld or unknown.
branches.cn: 名字未知或省略的物件。

branches.en: The event or matter waiting to be handled.
branches.cn: 等待处理的事件或事项。

branches.en: The plural that sums up a whole situation.
branches.cn: 概括整个局面的复数。

branches.en: Belongings gathered, and persons named by feeling.
branches.cn: 被收拢的物品，被情感指称的人。

branches.en: Object and event share one box: the old assembly decided matters, not mere objects.
branches.cn: 物与事共用一盒：古老的集会裁决的是事项，而非单纯的物件。

intro.en: Thing builds compounds with pronoun words, forming the backbone of English indefinite pronouns.
intro.cn: thing 与代词性成分构成复合词，撑起英语不定代词的骨架。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source; the compounds are native formations, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语来源；复合词均为本土构造，拉丁词条留空。

items.example: There is something in my shoe.

items.meaning: any object or matter at all
items.example: Is there anything cheaper?
Everything went as planned.
Nothing happened that night.
The trip was anything but relaxing.
I will not go; for one thing, it is too far.
The thing is, we have no time.
All things considered, the plan is sound.
items.exampleCN: 通盘考虑，这个计划是稳妥的。

definition_zh: 想；思考；认为；回想；打算
definition_en: to use the mind to form ideas, opinions, or plans, or to hold something as an opinion
core_image: 头脑里的工作台：想法在上面被拿起、翻看、装配
scene: 窗外下着雨,她盯着棋盘很久。Think before you move the knight.
sceneCN: 这里 think 是「思考」（第 1 个义项：用心智形成想法）；句意：走马之前先想一想。

pos.zh: 思考；想法（口语，如 have a think）

derivatives.zh: 想法；思想；思考（think 的过去式转名词）
思考；见解（think 的现在分词转名词）
思考者；思想家（think 加施动者后缀 -er）
深思的；体贴的（thought 加形容词后缀 -ful）

senses.title: To use the mind
senses.definition: to use the mind to form ideas, solve problems, or make decisions
senses.definitionCN: 运用头脑形成想法、解决问题或作出决定
senses.example: Give me a minute to think.
senses.exampleCN: 给我一分钟想一想。
senses.why: The core act: the mind works visibly hard, and the word simply names that work.
senses.whyCN: 核心行为：头脑明显地在劳作，这个词就是给这份劳作起名。

senses.title: To hold an opinion
senses.definition: to believe or hold something as an opinion, often less certain than know
senses.definitionCN: 相信或把某事当作看法，确定性低于 know
senses.example: I think the meeting starts at nine.
senses.exampleCN: 我想会议九点开始。
senses.why: An idea formed in the head is offered to the world as a claim; think marks the claim as personal and revisable.
senses.whyCN: 在头脑中形成的想法被作为主张交给世界；think 标记这主张属个人且可修正。

senses.title: To recall or imagine
senses.definition: to bring a past thing to mind, or to form a picture of something not present
senses.definitionCN: 让往事浮现心头，或构想不在眼前之物
senses.example: She still thinks of that summer by the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 她仍会想起海边那个夏天。
senses.why: The mind's workbench holds not only the present but the past and the possible; both arrive by the same act.
senses.whyCN: 头脑的工作台不只放当下，也放过去与可能；两者经由同一个动作到来。

senses.title: To intend or plan
senses.definition: to have a plan or intention in the mind, often in thinking of doing
senses.definitionCN: 心中存有计划或意图，常用于 thinking of doing
senses.example: We are thinking of moving to the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在考虑搬到海边住。
senses.why: A plan is an action rehearsed in the head before it happens; thinking is that rehearsal.
senses.whyCN: 计划是行动在头脑中的预演；thinking 就是这场预演。

senses.title: To expect or suppose
senses.definition: to expect or suppose that something will happen or is true
senses.definitionCN: 预期某事会发生或属实
senses.example: I think it will clear up by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 我料想到中午天会放晴。
senses.why: Opinion pointed forward becomes expectation: the same claim, wearing tomorrow's clothes.
senses.whyCN: 看法指向未来便成了预期：同一个主张，换上了明天的衣裳。

intro.en: Think is a native Germanic verb, and its strange past form thought preserves a very old sound pattern in which a t replaced the k of the present.
intro.cn: think 是日耳曼本土动词；其奇特的过去式 thought 保留了一种极古老的音变模式：过去式以 t 代替现在的 k。

items.en: The common Germanic root Thankjan meant to seem or to appear to the mind; the same root gave both think and seem in some relatives.
items.cn: 公认日耳曼词根 Thankjan 意为「在心中显现、似乎」；同一词根在部分亲属语言中既给出 think 也给出 seem 义。

items.en: Old English had two verbs: Thencan, to think in the modern sense, and Thyncan, to seem. Their past forms crossed and merged.
items.cn: 古英语有两个动词：Thencan（现代的「想」）与 Thyncan（「似乎」）；二者的过去式相互交叉并合流。

items.en: Middle English merged the two verbs into think with past thought, and the seeming sense faded away.
items.cn: 中古英语将两词合并为 think，过去式 thought，「似乎」义渐消。

items.en: Modern English fixed the paradigm think, thought and built a wide family: thinker, thoughtful, thoughtless, overthink.
items.cn: 现代英语固定 think-thought 范式，并衍生出 thinker、thoughtful、thoughtless、overthink 等庞大家族。

items.en: The noun think (have a think) and think tank show the verb moving into noun jobs in modern colloquial and institutional English.
items.cn: 名词 think（have a think）与 think tank 显示该动词在现代口语与机构用语中转任名词。

note.en: The first group is the think-thought family; the second compares verbs of mind work.
note.cn: 第一组是 think-thought 词族；第二组比较各种「心智劳作」动词。

entries.definition: past of think, and also the noun for an idea
entries.definitionCN: think 的过去式，也可作名词指想法

entries.definition: an object; shares most sounds with think but is a different word entirely
entries.definitionCN: 东西；与 think 读音相近，但完全是另一个词

entries.definition: to express gratitude; from a related Germanic root about inner feeling
entries.definitionCN: 感谢；出自关于内心感受的相关日耳曼词根

entries.definition: to accept something as true; stronger commitment than think
entries.definitionCN: 相信；比 think 承诺更强

entries.definition: to think about carefully before deciding
entries.definitionCN: 斟酌；决定前的仔细思考

entries.definition: to assume something is true without proof
entries.definitionCN: 假定；设想（无充分证据的认定）

normalIntro.en: Real hooks: the old t-past pattern, the think-thought family, and the difference between think and know.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：古老的 t 形过去式、think-thought 词族、以及 think 与 know 之别。

normal.en: Think, thought, thought: the k becomes ght in the past, an ancient fingerprint.
normal.cn: think 的过去式 thought：k 变 ght，是古老的指纹。

normal.en: I think softens a claim; I know hardens it.
normal.cn: I think 让主张变软，I know 让主张变硬。

normal.en: Think of recalls, think about studies, think over weighs.
normal.cn: think of 是想起，think about 是研究，think over 是掂量。

normal.en: A think tank is a tank full of thinking, not of fuel.
normal.cn: think tank 是装满思考的罐子，不是装燃料的。

normal.en: Thoughtful people think of others as well as of problems.
normal.cn: thoughtful 的人既想问题，也想别人。

abstract.en: Thinking is the rehearsal room where actions try their lines.
abstract.cn: 思考是排练厅，行动在里面练习台词。

abstract.en: Every thought is a small claim asking to be tested.
abstract.cn: 每个想法都是一桩等待检验的小主张。

abstract.en: The mind's workbench never quite empties.
abstract.cn: 头脑的工作台从不清空。

examples.en: She sat quietly, thinking about the offer.
examples.cn: 她静静坐着，考虑那份邀约。

examples.en: I thought the train left at noon, but it was three.
examples.cn: 我以为火车中午开，其实是三点。

examples.en: He thought carefully before answering.
examples.cn: 他仔细想过才回答。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯因克」——思考像沉进 sink（水槽）里打转 → think 思考

root: 日耳曼本土动词：词根 Thankjan「在心中显现」→ 古英语 Thencan「想」与 Thyncan「似乎」合流；过去式 thought 保留古音变（k→t 型）；同根亲族含 thank。

sensesIntro.en: Think works the mind in five directions: solving, opining, recalling, planning, and expecting, all from one image of ideas handled on an inner workbench.
sensesIntro.cn: think 让心智朝五个方向运作：解题、持论、追忆、筹划、预期——全部来自「内在工作台上摆弄想法」这一个意象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an inner workbench where ideas are picked up, turned over, and assembled.
core.cn: 核心意象：内在工作台，想法在上面被拿起、翻看、装配。

branches.en: The bare labour of the mind.
branches.cn: 心智的朴素劳作。

branches.en: A claim offered as personal and revisable.
branches.cn: 作为个人可修正意见提出的主张。

branches.en: The workbench reaching into past and possibility.
branches.cn: 伸向过去与可能的工作台。

branches.en: Actions rehearsed before they happen.
branches.cn: 行动发生前的预演。

branches.en: Opinion dressed for tomorrow.
branches.cn: 换上明天衣裳的看法。

intro.en: Think builds its family with small native endings and compounds, mostly through its past form thought.
intro.cn: think 用本土小词尾与复合词构建词族，大多经由其过去式 thought。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source; the family is native Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语来源；词族为日耳曼本土，拉丁词条留空。

items.meaning: past of think; also a noun for an idea
items.meaningCN: think 的过去式；名词「想法」
items.example: She thought it over; a thought struck her.
items.exampleCN: 她考虑了一下；忽然有了个想法。

items.meaning: the activity or opinions of thinking
items.example: His thinking changed after the course.
She is a clear thinker.
It was a thoughtful gift.

items.meaningCN: 欠考虑的；不顾及他人的
items.example: A thoughtless remark hurt her.
items.exampleCN: 一句欠考虑的话伤了她。

items.example: Stop overthinking the reply.
items.exampleCN: 别把那个回复想太多了。

items.meaning: a research organization full of ideas
items.example: The think tank published a housing report.
items.exampleCN: 该智库发布了住房报告。

items.meaningCN: 感谢（同根亲族，源于内心感受）
items.example: I thanked her twice.

definition_zh: 第三；三分之一；第三的
definition_en: coming after two others in order, or one of three equal parts
core_image: 队伍里数到三的那个人：前面已经站了两个
scene: 发令枪响,前两人冲得太猛,他在弯道反超。He finished third in the school race, his first medal.
sceneCN: 这里 third 是「第三名」（第 1 个义项：排序中位于两位之后）；句意：他在校运会上得了第三名，拿到第一块奖牌。

pos.zh: 三分之一；第三日；第三名

derivatives.zh: 三（third 的基数词，序数词 third 由其古形式加后缀构成）
第三（列举时用，加副词后缀 -ly）
三十（同根数词，three 的十倍形式）
十三（同根数词，three 加 -teen 构成）

senses.title: Position after two
senses.titleCN: 第三：排序中位于第三位
senses.definition: coming after two other people or things in order or rank
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序或等级排在另外两个之后
senses.example: This is her third attempt at the driving test.
senses.exampleCN: 这是她第三次考驾照。
senses.why: Counting names places, and third is the name of the place behind the first two.
senses.whyCN: 计数即命名位置，third 就是排在头两个之后那个位置的名字。

senses.title: One of three equal parts
senses.definition: one of three equal parts of something
senses.definitionCN: 把整体三等分后的一份
senses.example: A third of the students chose art.
senses.exampleCN: 三分之一的学生选了艺术。
senses.why: Cut the whole into three equal pieces and each piece inherits the number's name.
senses.whyCN: 把整体切成三等份，每份便继承了这个数字的名字。

senses.title: Grammar: third person
senses.definition: the grammatical category for someone or something spoken about, not spoken to
senses.definitionCN: 语法范畴，指被谈论而非被交谈的人或物
senses.example: Write the story in the third person.
senses.exampleCN: 用第三人称写这个故事。
senses.why: Grammar borrows the queue: I stand first, you stand second, everyone else waits third.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了队列：我站第一，你站第二，其余人都排在第三。

senses.title: Music and angles
senses.definition: a musical interval of three scale steps, or a fraction of a turn or angle
senses.definitionCN: 三个音级构成的音程，或转角的三等分之一
senses.example: The chord is built on a third.
senses.exampleCN: 这个和弦建立在三度音上。
senses.why: Music and geometry both count steps, so the ordinal steps in whenever three positions are measured.
senses.whyCN: 音乐与几何都在数步子，凡度量三个位置之处，序数词便登场。

intro.en: Third looks like three plus th, but it is really the older of the two forms: its root thr- is the ancient Germanic shape that three itself later wore down from.
intro.cn: third 看似 three 加 th，其实它才是更古老的形式：其词根 thr- 是古老的日耳曼形状，three 本身正是从中磨损演变而来。

items.en: The root Thriz, generally reconstructed, meant three; the th- shape is older than the th- of three.
items.cn: 公认词根一般重构为 Thriz，意为「三」；其 th- 形状比 three 的 th- 更古老。

items.en: Old English Thridda (or Thirda) meant third, keeping the old thr- intact.
items.cn: 古英语 Thridda (or Thirda) 意为「第三」，完整保留了古老的 thr-。

items.en: Norse Thrithi (or Thridi) was the name of a god, The Third, and the cousin form pressed on English usage.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 Thrithi (or Thridi) 是一位神的名字「第三者」，其同源形式也影响着英语用法。

items.en: Middle English metathesis slid the r around: thridda became thrid and then third, trading letters like cards.
items.cn: 中古英语的音位交换挪动了 r 的位置：thridda 变成 thrid 再变 third，字母像纸牌一样换了位。

items.en: Modern English settled third with 3rd as its short form, and the grammar terms third person and third party became everyday phrases.
items.cn: 现代英语固定了 third（缩写 3rd），third person 与 third party 等语法术语成为日常短语。

note.en: The first group holds the counting family around three; the second compares the ordinals and their kin.
note.cn: 第一组是围绕「三」的数词家族；第二组比较序数词及其近亲。

entries.definition: the cardinal number; third is its ordinal

definition_zh: 渴的；口干的；渴望的；干旱的
definition_en: feeling a need to drink, or wanting something very much
core_image: 喉咙里像塞了一把干沙：整个身体在喊水
scene: 足球赛下半场,他扶着膝盖大口喘气。The thirsty players lined up at the water table after the match.
sceneCN: 这里 thirsty 是「口渴的」（第 1 个义项：身体需要喝水）；句意：赛后口渴的球员们在饮水台前排起了队。

pos.zh: 渴望的；饥渴的（与 for 连用）

senses.title: Needing to drink
senses.definition: feeling the need or wish to drink water
senses.definitionCN: 感到需要或想喝水
senses.example: The long climb left everyone thirsty.
senses.exampleCN: 长途攀登让每个人都渴了。
senses.why: The body speaks through the throat: dryness there is the whole message, and thirsty is its word.
senses.whyCN: 身体借喉咙发言：那里的干涩就是全部讯息，thirsty 便是这讯息的词。

senses.title: Strongly wanting something
senses.definition: having a strong desire for something, usually with for
senses.definitionCN: 对某物有强烈渴望，通常与 for 连用
senses.example: Fresh from school, she was thirsty for real work.
senses.exampleCN: 刚出校门的她渴望真正的工作。
senses.why: The dry throat becomes the picture of any hunger of the mind: what the body feels for water, the soul feels for its goals.
senses.whyCN: 干渴的喉咙成为一切精神饥饿的图景：身体之于水，正如灵魂之于目标。

senses.title: Dry land or climate
senses.definition: (of land, plants, or weather) dry and needing water
senses.definitionCN: 指土地、植物或气候干燥缺水
senses.example: The thirsty field cracked under the August sun.
senses.exampleCN: 八月的烈日下，干渴的田地裂了缝。
senses.why: The word climbs out of the throat and into the landscape: earth that cannot drink is described with the body's word.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从喉咙爬进风景：喝不上水的土地，用身体的词来描述。

senses.title: Causing thirst
senses.definition: causing thirst, as in hard physical work or a hot task
senses.definitionCN: 引起口渴的，如重体力劳动或炎热的工作
senses.example: Digging the well was thirsty work.
senses.exampleCN: 挖井是件让人口渴的活儿。
senses.why: English turns the feeling around: work that makes you thirsty can itself be called thirsty.
senses.whyCN: 英语把这感觉掉了个头：让人口渴的活儿，本身也可以被称作口渴的。

intro.en: Thirsty is the adjective of thirst, and thirst is a native Germanic word for the burning dryness of the throat, cousin to words for scorched land in the old languages.
intro.cn: thirsty 是 thirst 的形容词；thirst 是日耳曼本土词，指喉咙灼人的干渴，在古语言中与表示焦土的词是亲戚。

items.en: The root Thurstu, generally reconstructed, meant dryness and the craving it causes, related to a root for scorched or dried up.
items.cn: 公认词根一般重构为 Thurstu，意为干渴及其引发的渴求，与表示「烧焦、晒干」的词根相关。

items.en: Old English Thurst (or Thurst) was the noun thirst, and Thurstig (or Thyrstig) the adjective thirsty.
items.cn: 古英语 Thurst (or Thurst) 是名词「渴」，Thurstig (or Thyrstig) 是形容词「渴的」。

items.en: Norse Thyrstr reinforced the northern forms with the same burning picture.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 Thyrstr 以同样的灼烧图景支持了北方形式。

items.en: Middle English thirst and thirsty spread into moral and religious writing, where thirst for righteousness became a standing image.
items.cn: 中古英语 thirst 与 thirsty 进入道德与宗教写作，「渴慕正义」成为固定意象。

items.en: Modern English kept thirsty for body, mind and land alike, and the compound bloodthirsty pushed the metaphor into darker ground.
items.cn: 现代英语让 thirsty 同时服务于身体、心灵与土地，复合词 bloodthirsty 则把比喻推向更暗处。

note.en: The first group holds the thirst family; the second compares the words of wanting and dryness.
note.cn: 第一组是 thirst 词族；第二组比较表示渴求与干燥的词。

entries.definitionCN: 十三；开头读音与 thirsty 相近，但表数目不表干渴

normalIntro.en: Real hooks: the scorched-earth root, the thirst-thirsty pair, and the thirst for image.

normal.en: Thirst is the feeling; thirsty is the throat that has it.

normal.en: Thirsty for knowledge: the mind has a throat too.

abstract.en: Desire learned its grammar from the throat.
abstract.cn: 欲望的语法是从喉咙学来的。

abstract.en: A thirsty field and a thirsty reader crack the same way.

senses.title: The number after twelve
senses.definition: the number 13, made of ten and three

senses.definitionCN: 由十三个人或物组成的一组

senses.whyCN: 数目一旦存在，被数的人群便借它作为整组的名字。

senses.title: The unlucky number
senses.definition: the number traditionally considered unlucky in Western culture
senses.definitionCN: 西方文化中传统上被视为不吉利的数字
senses.example: They renumbered the floors to avoid thirteen.
senses.exampleCN: 他们重新编排楼层号以避开十三。
senses.why: Custom attaches feelings to numbers, and thirteen carries the heaviest baggage of them all.
senses.whyCN: 习俗给数字附加情感，而十三背负的行囊最重。

intro.en: Thirteen is pure Germanic arithmetic: the old form of three plus teen, a shortened word for ten, spoken as one number since before written English.
intro.cn: thirteen 是纯粹的日耳曼算术：three 的古形式加 teen（ten 的缩略形式），在书面英语出现之前就已作为一个数字被念出。

items.en: Germanic numbers from thirteen to nineteen were built the same way: the digit word plus a form of ten.
items.cn: 日耳曼语的十三至十九都以同一方式构成：个位数词加一个 ten 的形式。

items.en: Old English Threotine (or Threotiene) joined threo (or thrie) (three) with tine (oriene) (ten), already one spoken word.
items.cn: 古英语 Threotine (or Threotiene) 把 threo (or thrie)（三）与 tine (oriene)（十）连成一个口语词。

items.en: Norse Threttan pressed on the northern English forms and helped fix the double t spelling pattern.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 Threttan 影响了英格兰北部形式，帮助固定了双写 t 的拼写格局。

items.en: Middle English Threttene (or Thirtene) settled the stress on the last part, which still marks all the teen numbers today.
items.cn: 中古英语 Threttene (or Thirtene) 把重音落在后半部，今天所有 -teen 数词仍保留这一特征。

items.en: Modern English wrote thirteen, and the number picked up its unlucky reputation in later Western folklore and building customs.
items.cn: 现代英语定型为 thirteen；这个数字在后来的西方民俗与建筑习俗中获得了不吉的名声。

note.en: The first group holds the -teen counting family; the second compares thirteen with its nearest sound relations.

core_image: 第十三级台阶：踩上去之前,你已数过十二级
scene: 旧旅馆的电梯键从十二跳到十四,只剩楼梯忠实如一。He climbed to the thirteenth floor by the stairs.
sceneCN: 这里 thirteenth 是「第十三」（第 1 个义项：排序中的位置）；句意：他走楼梯上了第十三层。

derivatives.zh: 十三（thirteenth 的基数词基础）

senses.title: Position after twelve
senses.definition: coming after twelve other people or things in order
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序排在另外十二个之后
senses.example: Her office is on the thirteenth floor.
senses.exampleCN: 她的办公室在第十三层。
senses.why: The ordinal pins the number to a place in the line: not thirteen of them, but the one at position thirteen.
senses.whyCN: 序数词把数字钉在线上的一个位置：不是十三个，而是第十三位的那一个。

senses.title: A date: the thirteenth day
senses.titleCN: 十三日：每月的第十三天
senses.definition: the thirteenth day of a month
senses.definitionCN: 一个月中的第十三天
senses.example: The lease begins on the thirteenth of May.
senses.exampleCN: 租约从五月十三日开始。
senses.why: Calendars are queues of days, and the ordinal names your place in the month's line.
senses.whyCN: 日历就是日子的队列，序数词标出你在月份长队中的位置。

senses.title: One of thirteen equal parts
senses.definition: one of thirteen equal parts of a whole
senses.definitionCN: 整体十三等分后的一份
senses.example: Each heir received a thirteenth of the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 每位继承人得到遗产的十三分之一。
senses.why: Cut the whole into thirteen and each slice inherits the ordinal's name, as with third and fourth.
senses.whyCN: 把整体切成十三份，每份便继承序数词之名，如 third、fourth 一般。

intro.en: Thirteenth is thirteen wearing the old ordinal ending -th, a suffix so ancient that it already worked on number words in the first Germanic songs.
intro.cn: thirteenth 就是 thirteen 加上古老的序数后缀 -th；这个后缀极其古老，在最早的日耳曼歌谣里就已作用于数词。

items.en: Germanic built ordinals with a -tha (or -da) ending on the number stem, a habit kept across all the daughter languages.
items.cn: 日耳曼语在数词词干上加 -tha (or -da) 构成序数词，这一习惯在各支语言中保留至今。

items.en: Old English Threoteotha (or Threoteotha) joined the teen number with the ordinal ending.
items.cn: 古英语 Threoteotha 把 -teen 数词与序数后缀连成一体。

items.en: Middle English Threttenthe (or Threttenthe) followed the settled form of thirteen and added the simplified -th.
items.cn: 中古英语 Threttenthe 在 thirteen 的定型形式上加简化后的 -th。

items.en: Modern English fixed thirteenth, the heaviest mouthful among the teens, with 13th as the friendly short form.
items.cn: 现代英语定型 thirteenth——-teen 数词中最拗口的一个——缩写 13th 更为顺口。

items.en: The date sense spread with printed calendars, where the thirteenth of the month carried its unlucky folklore.
items.cn: 随印刷日历普及，日期义传播开来，每月十三号也背上了不吉的民俗。

note.en: The first group lines up the ordinal against its base and neighbours; the second gathers the century and date companions.
note.cn: 第一组将序数词与其基数及相邻序数并列；第二组是世纪与日期中的同伴。

definition_zh: 第三十；第三十的；三十分之一
definition_en: coming after twenty-nine others in order, or one of thirty equal parts
core_image: 日历翻过二十九页,停在第三十页
scene: 银婚之后又熬过几年风雨,亲友们围在老屋门口。They celebrated their thirtieth wedding anniversary with the whole street.
sceneCN: 这里 thirtieth 是「第三十」（第 1 个义项：排序或周年计数）；句意：他们与整条街的邻居一起庆祝了三十周年结婚纪念日。

senses.title: Position after twenty-nine
senses.titleCN: 第三十：排在二十九之后
senses.definition: coming after twenty-nine other people or things in order
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序排在另外二十九个之后
senses.example: She is the thirtieth patient on the waiting list.
senses.exampleCN: 她是候诊名单上的第三十位病人。
senses.why: The ordinal is the number with a place in line; thirtieth holds position thirty no matter how long the queue grows.
senses.whyCN: 序数词是排好位置的数字；无论队伍多长，thirtieth 都守住第三十位。

senses.title: A thirtieth part
senses.definition: one of thirty equal parts of a whole
senses.definitionCN: 整体三十等分后的一份
senses.example: Each of the thirty heirs got a thirtieth share.
senses.exampleCN: 三十位继承人各得三十分之一。
senses.why: Cut the whole into thirty equal pieces and the ordinal lends its name to each piece.
senses.whyCN: 把整体切成三十等份，序数词便把名字借给每一份。

senses.title: Anniversary and date
senses.definition: the thirtieth occurrence of a yearly event, or the thirtieth day of a month
senses.definitionCN: 年度事件的第三十次发生，或一个月的第三十天
senses.example: The band marked its thirtieth year with a farewell tour.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队以告别巡演纪念成立三十周年。
senses.why: Repeating events are counted like positions in a line: the thirtieth anniversary is year thirty of the queue.
senses.whyCN: 循环事件像队列中的位置一样被计数：三十周年就是这条长队中的第三十个年头。

intro.en: Thirtieth is thirty, itself an old compound of the digit three and a word for ten, wearing the ordinal ending -th at the end of a long line of counting history.
intro.cn: thirtieth 的基础是 thirty——它本身是数字 three 与「十」的古老复合词——再戴上序数后缀 -th，走完一段悠长的计数史。

items.en: Germanic built tens by attaching the digit word to a fixed form of ten: three plus ten became thirty.
items.cn: 日耳曼语把个位数词接到固定的「十」形式上构成整十数：三加十成为 thirty。

items.en: Old English Thritig (or Thritig) meant thirty, and Thritigotha (or Thritigotha) its ordinal thirtieth.
items.cn: 古英语 Thritig (or Thritig) 意为三十，Thritigotha (or Thritigotha) 为其序数「第三十」。

items.en: Norse Thritugu (or Thritugu) supported the same tens pattern in the north.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 Thritugu (or Thritugu) 在北方支持着同样的整十数模式。

items.en: Middle English Thirty shortened the ending, and Thirtithe (or Thirtithe) smoothed the ordinal's spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语 Thirty 缩短了词尾，Thirtithe (or Thirtithe) 顺平了序数词的拼写。

items.en: Modern English settled thirtieth with 30th as its short form, the y of thirty changing to ieth as the suffix settled in.
items.cn: 现代英语定型 thirtieth（缩写 30th），thirty 的 y 因后缀进入而变为 ieth。

note.en: The first group separates the thirtieth-thirteenth sound tangle; the second lines up the tens ordinals.
note.cn: 第一组解开 thirtieth 与 thirteenth 的读音纠缠；第二组排列整十序数词。

senses.title: The number thirty

intro.en: Thirty is plain Germanic arithmetic frozen into one word: the old form of three plus a fixed ending that once meant ten, worn smooth by centuries of speech.
intro.cn: thirty 是被冻结成单词的日耳曼算术：three 的古形式加上曾表示「十」的固定词尾，经数百年口语磨得光滑。

items.en: Germanic formed its tens with the digit plus Thig (or Teguh), a form of ten, so three plus ten made the word for thirty.
items.cn: 日耳曼语用个位数加 Thig (or Teguh)（ten 的形式）构成整十数，三加十即为三十之词。

items.en: Old English Thritig (or Thritig) was already one word, used for counts of people, days and money.
items.cn: 古英语 Thritig (or Thritig) 已是一个词，用于数人、数日、数钱。

items.en: Norse Thrir Tigr (or Thrir Tigr) still said it in two parts, three tens, showing the arithmetic behind the English single word.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 Thrir Tigr (or Thrir Tigr) 仍分两部分说「三个十」，展示了英语单词背后的算术。

items.en: Middle English wore the word down to Thirty, the ending shrinking as speech quickened.
items.cn: 中古英语把词磨成 Thirty，词尾随语速加快而缩短。

items.en: Modern English fixed thirty, built its plural the thirties for ages and decades, and paired it with ordinal thirtieth.
items.cn: 现代英语定型 thirty，派生 the thirties 表示岁数与年代，并配上序数词 thirtieth。

abstract.en: The thirties of a life are its first full adult decade.
abstract.cn: 人生的三十多岁是第一个完整的成年十年。

abstract.en: Every decade of history borrows the counting of hands.
abstract.cn: 历史的每个十年都借用了手指的计数。

examples.en: The class has thirty desks.
examples.cn: 教室里有三十张课桌。

examples.en: She ran thirty kilometres without stopping.
examples.cn: 她不停顿地跑了三十公里。

examples.en: Prices rose by thirty per cent in a year.
examples.cn: 一年内物价上涨了百分之三十。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑟提」——三十而立,「瑟瑟」发抖也要「提」起精神 → thirty 三十

root: 日耳曼整十数合成词：three 古形式 + -tig（「十的倍数」固定词尾）→ 古英语 Thritig (or Thritig) → 中古英语磨为 Thirty → 现代 thirty；复数 thirties 表岁数与年代。

sensesIntro.en: Thirty counts things first, then ages and decades, giving English its word for both a stretch of life and a stretch of history.
sensesIntro.cn: thirty 先数物，再数年龄与年代，为英语同时提供了一段人生与一段历史的称呼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three bundles of ten, tied and counted as one number.
core.cn: 核心意象：三捆各十的箭束，捆好并作一个数来数。

branches.en: The plain number for counting.
branches.cn: 用于计数的朴素数字。

branches.en: The first full adult decade of a life.
branches.cn: 人生第一个完整的成年十年。

branches.en: A named stretch of a century.
branches.cn: 世纪中一段有名有姓的时期。

branches.en: Both borrow the number for a stretch of time.
branches.cn: 两者都借这个数字来称一段时间。

branches.en: Arithmetic visible in the spelling: three plus ten.
branches.cn: 拼写下可见的算术：三加十。

intro.en: Thirty heads the -ty tens family for the thirties, and its ordinal shifts the y to ieth.
intro.cn: thirty 领衔三十段的 -ty 整十数家族，其序数词把 y 变为 ieth。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source; the counting system is native Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语来源；计数体系为日耳曼本土，拉丁词条留空。

items.meaningCN: 构成整十数（十的老形式）
items.example: Six, sixty; seven, seventy.
items.exampleCN: six 变 sixty；seven 变 seventy。

items.example: Thirty miles to go.
Her thirtieth year abroad.
items.exampleCN: 她在国外的第三十个年头。

items.meaning: ages or years thirty to thirty-nine
items.example: The swing music of the thirties.
Twenty questions, one answer.
Forty winks before dinner.
Thirteen is not thirty.
Jazz flourished in the nineteen-thirties.
items.exampleCN: 爵士乐在二十世纪三十年代兴盛。

definition_zh: 这；这个；这样的事；此刻；这么
definition_en: used to point at a person or thing near in place, time, or thought
core_image: 伸手可及处的那一个：近处的手指
scene: 他把车钥匙递到你掌心,金属还带着温度。Hold this while I lock the door.
sceneCN: 这里 this 是「这个」（第 1 个义项：指近处的物）；句意：我锁门时你拿一下这个。

derivatives.zh: 这些（this 的复数形式）
那；那个（this 的远指对应词）
如此；因而（同族指示副词，正式用语）
从那里（同族 there 系列正式词）

senses.title: The near one
senses.titleCN: 这；这个：指近处的人或物
senses.definition: used to point at a person or thing that is near in place or just being held or shown
senses.definitionCN: 指向空间上近处或正被拿着、展示的人或物
senses.example: This book is the one I told you about.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书就是我跟你说的那本。
senses.why: Every pointing pair needs a near pole; this is the finger curled toward the speaker's own side.
senses.whyCN: 每对指示词都需要近端；this 就是朝说话者一侧弯回的那根手指。

senses.title: The present time
senses.definition: used with time words to mean the current day, week, or moment
senses.definitionCN: 与时间词连用，表示今天、本周或此刻
senses.example: This week has gone far too fast.
senses.exampleCN: 这一周过得太快了。
senses.why: Time is mapped onto space: the moment you stand in is near, so the near pointer marks it.
senses.whyCN: 时间被映射到空间上：你立足的时刻是「近」的，近指词便落在它身上。

senses.title: Introducing something new
senses.titleCN: 引出新话题：以下要说的
senses.definition: used to refer to something about to be said or introduced in a story
senses.definitionCN: 指即将说出或故事中即将登场的事物
senses.example: Now this is the interesting part of the recipe.
senses.exampleCN: 现在来看这个食谱最有趣的部分。
senses.why: Before the audience can see the thing, the speaker plants the pointer in the empty spot ahead.
senses.whyCN: 在观众看清事物之前，说话者先把手指插进前方空位。

senses.title: To this degree
senses.definition: to the degree or amount shown, as in this big or this far
senses.definitionCN: 达到所指的程度或数量，如 this big、this far
senses.example: I didn't know the lake was this deep.
senses.exampleCN: 我不知道这湖有这么深。
senses.why: The pointing hand can measure: the distance between two palms becomes the size of the word.
senses.whyCN: 指示的手也能量度：两只手掌之间的距离变成了词的大小。

intro.en: This is a native English demonstrative built on the ancient stem tha- that also gave the, that, they and there; it has pointed at near things for as long as English has existed.
intro.cn: this 是本土英语指示词，建立在古老词干 tha- 之上；the、that、they、there 都出自这个词干。英语存在多久，它就指了多久的近物。

items.en: The Germanic demonstrative stem Tha- produced the whole pointing system: articles, pronouns and place words.
items.cn: 日耳曼指示词干 Tha- 产出整套指示系统：冠词、代词与地点词。

items.en: Old English This (or This) served for all genders of the near demonstrative, alongside the (feminine) and that (neuter).
items.cn: 古英语 This (or This) 作近指代词用于各个性别，与 the（阴性）、that（中性）并行。

items.en: Norse Thessi (or Thessi) kept a similar near form, and contact reinforced the English system.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 Thessi (or Thessi) 保有相近的近指形式，语言接触加固了英语体系。

items.en: Middle English paired this with that as the neat near-far duo, and these took over the plural.
items.cn: 中古英语把 this 与 that 配成整洁的近远对，these 接管了复数。

items.en: Modern English extended this to time, to story introductions, and to degree, making it one of the most frequent words in the language.
items.cn: 现代英语把 this 扩展到时间、故事引入与程度，使之成为英语最高频词之一。

note.en: The first group holds the pointing system this belongs to; the second gathers its near partners in grammar.
note.cn: 第一组是 this 所属的指示系统；第二组是语法中的近指伙伴。

entries.definition: the plural of this, for several near things
entries.definitionCN: 这些（this 的复数，指近处的多个）

entries.definition: the far-side partner of the near pointer
entries.definitionCN: 那；那个（远指，与近指相对）

entries.definition: in this way; the adverb cousin in the pointing family
entries.definitionCN: 如此；因而（指示词族的副词近亲）

entries.definition: in this place; the adverb built on the same near idea
entries.definitionCN: 在这里；同一近指观念的地点副词

entries.definition: the definite article, the worn-down member of the same family
entries.definitionCN: 定冠词；同一家族磨蚀最重的成员

normalIntro.en: Real hooks: the tha- stem family, the near-far pair, and this as measure word.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：tha- 词干家族、近远对立、以及 this 的量度用法。

normal.en: This is near, that is far: one vowel length apart.
normal.cn: this 近，that 远：一个元音长度之差。

normal.en: This morning, this week: time near you takes the near pointer.
normal.cn: this morning、this week：靠近你的时间用近指词。

normal.en: These books are this heavy: plural shape, degree job.
normal.cn: these books are this heavy：复数形与程度义各司其职。

normal.en: The, this, that, they, there: one ancient stem runs them all.
normal.cn: the、this、that、they、there：同一古老词干统领。

normal.en: This deep: the hand measures and the word reports.
normal.cn: this deep：手在量，词在报数。

abstract.en: This is the speaker's side of the world made into a word.
abstract.cn: this 是把世界的「说话者一侧」做成的词。

abstract.en: Nearness is a place before it is a time.
abstract.cn: 「近」先是地点，然后才是时间。

abstract.en: Every conversation begins by planting this in the shared ground.
abstract.cn: 每场对话都从把 this 插进共同地面开始。

examples.en: This is my favourite chair.
examples.cn: 这是我最喜欢的椅子。

examples.en: I have lived here all this time.
examples.cn: 我一直住在这里，始终如此。

examples.en: It isn't this cold every winter.
examples.cn: 并不是每个冬天都这么冷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞斯」——东西就在手边,一伸手就「瑞斯（于是）」拿到了 → this 这个

root: 本土指示词：日耳曼词干 Tha-（与 the、that、they、there 同源）→ 古英语 This (or This)「近指」→ 中古英语与 that 配成近远对；复数 these；程度义后起。

sensesIntro.en: This points at the near object, claims the present moment, introduces what comes next, and finally measures how much.
sensesIntro.cn: this 先指近处的物，再占有当下时刻，引入即将登场者，最后丈量程度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger curled back toward the speaker's own side.
core.cn: 核心意象：朝说话者一侧弯回的手指。

branches.en: The near pole of the pointing pair.
branches.cn: 指示对的近端。

branches.en: The moment the speaker stands in.
branches.cn: 说话者立足的时刻。

branches.en: The pointer set before the thing arrives.
branches.cn: 事物登场前插下的指示牌。

branches.en: The hand stretched into a ruler.
branches.cn: 伸开成标尺的手。

branches.en: Both rest on nearness: of hand or of moment.
branches.cn: 两者都立于「近」：手之近或时之近。

intro.en: This belongs to the tha- demonstrative family, the most productive native system in English grammar.
intro.cn: this 属于 tha- 指示词家族，这是英语语法中能产性最强的本土体系。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source; the family is native Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语来源；家族为日耳曼本土，拉丁词条留空。

items.example: These apples are sweeter.
That hill hides a cave.
Those clouds mean rain.
Thus the matter was settled.
The book on the desk is mine.

items.meaningCN: 他们；它们（同词干复数代词）
items.example: They arrived at dawn.
Come here, please.
Two miles hence stands the mill.

definition_zh: 彻底的；全面的；仔细的；彻头彻尾的
definition_en: done completely, with every part attended to and nothing left out
core_image: 把抽屉整个抽出来翻到底：一件东西都不放过
scene: 海关的探员把行李箱翻了个底朝天,连衬里都摸过。The officer gave the suitcase a thorough search before returning it.
sceneCN: 这里 thorough 是「彻底的」（第 1 个义项：每个细节都检查到）；句意：关员把行李箱彻底搜查了一遍才归还。

derivatives.zh: 彻底地；非常（thorough 加副词后缀 -ly）
彻底；周密（thorough 加名词后缀 -ness）
大道；通路（thorough 加 fare 复合，指通行之路）
穿过；通过（与 thorough 同源近亲，易混词）

senses.title: Complete, missing nothing
senses.definition: including every possible part or detail, with nothing missed
senses.definitionCN: 涵盖每个可能的部位或细节，无所遗漏
senses.example: The doctor carried out a thorough examination.
senses.exampleCN: 医生做了全面检查。
senses.why: The word sees the job as a road: a thorough job is one that has gone all the way through.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把工作看作一条路：彻底的工作就是把路走穿到底的工作。

senses.title: Careful and painstaking
senses.definition: taking care to do things properly and in detail, of a person or their manner
senses.definitionCN: 指人或其作风认真细致，务必做好每个环节
senses.example: She is thorough in everything she signs.
senses.exampleCN: 她签每份文件都一丝不苟。
senses.why: A person can inherit the road image: someone whose attention walks every step of the way.
senses.whyCN: 人也能继承道路意象：其注意力走完路上的每一步。

senses.title: Out-and-out, complete in kind
senses.definition: complete or absolute in kind, often of an undesirable quality
senses.definitionCN: 在性质上完全的、绝对的，常指不好的品质
senses.example: The scheme was a thorough failure.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划彻底失败了。
senses.why: Completeness does not judge: if a thing fails through and through, thorough reports the depth of it.
senses.whyCN: 彻底不问好坏：一件事从头败到尾，thorough 报告的只是失败的深度。

intro.en: Thorough is the adjective twin of through: the same old word for moving from one side to the other, split by spelling into a preposition of motion and an adjective of completeness.
intro.cn: thorough 是 through 的形容词孪生兄弟：同一个表示「从一侧到另一侧」的古词，经拼写分化为表运动的介词与表彻底的形容词。

items.en: The root Thurh (or Thurh) meant through, from one side to the other, built on old words for door or passage.
items.cn: 词根 Thurh (or Thurh) 意为「穿过」，从一侧到另一侧，出自表示「门、通道」的古词。

items.en: Old English Thurh (or Thurh) worked as preposition and adverb, and the compound Thurhborh (or Thyrhborh) meant going right through, hence complete.
items.cn: 古英语 Thurh (or Thurh) 兼作介词与副词，复合词 Thurhborh (or Thyrhborh) 意为「直贯而过」，引申为完全。

items.en: Middle English split the spellings: through kept the motion job, and thorough took the completeness job.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写分化：through 保留运动义，thorough 接管彻底义。

items.en: The compound thoroughfare named a road that goes through, first for people, later for traffic.
items.cn: 复合词 thoroughfare 指可以贯穿而过的路，先指人行，后指车马。

items.en: Modern English settled the pair, and thorough became the standard word for complete care in work, study and examination.
items.cn: 现代英语固定了这对词，thorough 成为工作、学习、检查中「彻底用心」的标准词。

note.en: The first group separates the thorough-through spelling pair; the second compares words of completeness and care.
note.cn: 第一组区分 thorough 与 through 的拼写纠缠；第二组比较表示彻底与用心的词。

entries.definition: from one side to the other; the motion twin of thorough
entries.definitionCN: 穿过；通过（thorough 的运动义孪生词）

entries.definition: a public road that passes through a place
entries.definitionCN: 大道；通行之路（thorough + fare）

entries.definition: although; one letter from through and often mistyped for thorough
entries.definitionCN: 虽然；拼写与 through 一字之差，常与 thorough 误输

entries.definition: having all its parts; finished
entries.definitionCN: 完整的；全部完成的

entries.definition: paying great attention to small details
entries.definitionCN: 一丝不苟的；对细节极为用心

entries.definition: covering all possibilities completely
entries.definitionCN: 穷尽的；涵盖一切可能的

normalIntro.en: Real hooks: the through twin, the road image inside the word, and the thoroughfare compound.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：through 孪生词、词内的道路意象、以及 thoroughfare 复合词。

normal.en: Thorough is through wearing an adjective's coat.
normal.cn: thorough 是穿上形容词外衣的 through。

normal.en: A thorough search goes through everything.
normal.cn: 彻底的搜查会把每样东西都翻 through。

normal.en: A thoroughfare is a road that goes through a town.
normal.cn: thoroughfare 是穿过城镇的路。

normal.en: Though, through, thorough: three spellings that trip every learner.
normal.cn: though、through、thorough：绊倒每个学习者的三种拼法。

normal.en: A thorough failure fails through and through.
normal.cn: 彻底的失败是从头到尾都失败。

abstract.en: Thorough is motion that refuses to stop halfway.
abstract.cn: thorough 是拒绝半途而废的运动。

abstract.en: Care that walks the whole road is called thorough.
abstract.cn: 走完整条路的用心，名为彻底。

abstract.en: Nothing thorough is ever done by halves.
abstract.cn: 彻底之事从无半途。

examples.en: Give the kitchen a thorough cleaning before the holiday.
examples.cn: 节日前把厨房彻底打扫一遍。

examples.en: The report is thorough, every figure checked twice.
examples.cn: 报告很周密，每个数字都核对了两遍。

examples.en: Their victory was a thorough one.
examples.cn: 他们的胜利是彻头彻尾的胜利。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑟若」——彻底检查,连一「丝」缝隙都「若」在眼前 → thorough 彻底的

root: 与 through 同源的孪生词：日耳曼词根 Thurh (or Thurh)「贯穿」→ 古英语复合词「直贯而过」引申「完全」→ 中古英语拼写分化：through 表运动，thorough 表彻底。

sensesIntro.en: Thorough takes the road image of through and turns it into completeness: the job gone all the way, the person who walks every step, the failure through and through.
sensesIntro.cn: thorough 把 through 的道路意象转化为彻底：走到底的工作、走满每一步的人、彻头彻尾的失败。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road walked from gate to gate without a shortcut.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从大门走到尽头、绝不抄近路的路。

branches.en: The complete job, nothing skipped.
branches.cn: 完整的工作，无一遗漏。

branches.en: The person whose care walks every step.
branches.cn: 用心走满每一步的人。

branches.en: Depth of a quality, good or bad.
branches.cn: 性质的深度，无论好坏。

branches.en: Both keep the road: one for the task, one for the walker.
branches.cn: 两者都保留道路：一个给任务，一个给行人。

branches.en: Completeness applied to failure doubles its weight.
branches.cn: 彻底用于失败，分量加倍。

intro.en: Thorough carries native endings lightly: -ly and -ness, plus the old compound thoroughfare.
intro.cn: thorough 轻装佩挂本土词尾：-ly 与 -ness，外加古老的复合词 thoroughfare。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source; the word is native Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语来源；本词为日耳曼本土，拉丁词条留空。

items.example: The house was thoroughly cleaned.
Her thoroughness saved the project.

items.meaning: a public road through a place
items.example: Oxford Street is a busy thoroughfare.
items.exampleCN: 牛津街是一条繁忙的大道。

items.meaning: from one side to the other
items.example: We drove through the tunnel.
The theme runs throughout the novel.
items.exampleCN: 这一主题贯穿整部小说。

items.example: A complete set of tools.
Meticulous notes marked his work.
items.exampleCN: 一丝不苟的笔记是他工作的印记。

items.meaningCN: 体贴的；深思的（读音对照）
items.example: A thoughtful reply ended the argument.
items.exampleCN: 一番体贴的回应结束了争执。
